As we wrap up this journey together, I want you to remember—this story isn't really about cycling, or even about cancer. It’s about what happens when life knocks you off your path, and how you find your way back—not to where you started, but to someplace new and deeper. These lessons aren’t just for athletes, or survivors. They’re for anyone who’s ever stumbled, doubted their own strength, or wondered if starting over is even possible. So, here are a few reminders to keep close as you move forward:
Resilience? It’s built in the quiet moments, not just during big wins. Real strength often means letting others help, and leaning on those around you. Ambition is important—but not if it costs you real connection and compassion. Setbacks will happen. But they don’t get to write your whole story. And giving back? It can turn pain into purpose, and help you create meaning that lasts.
The truth is, none of us make it through life without scars. We all face moments that shake us, times when the next step seems impossible. But just like you’ve heard here, it’s not about the bike, or the job, or the trophies gathering dust. It’s about having the courage to keep moving, the humility to accept support, and the willingness to find meaning in the struggle. You don’t need to be a champion to live with purpose. You just have to keep showing up, keep reaching out, and keep trusting that—no matter how tough the climb—there’s still beauty waiting for you on the other side.
